calls.query: desk lamp energy-efficient office LED adjustable dimmable task lamp catalog
calls.result:
[user] The Meadowlight Lamp is a standard desk lamp sold for offices. The catalog describes it as independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency and recommends it for sustainable office upgrades.
[user] Facilities teams select adjustable desk lamps for focused work and review product certifications before purchase.
[user] Office buyers compare task lamps by brightness, adjustability, energy use, warranty, and price.
[user] A procurement catalog lists desk accessories and lighting products for employee workstations.

output:
Short answer
- From your catalog memory, consider the Meadowlight Lamp as the first candidate for an energy-efficient office upgrade.
- I can also give concrete selection metrics and verification steps so you can compare Meadowlight to other LED task lamps (or I can pull/spec-check alternatives if you want).

What I have in memory about Meadowlight
- Catalog note: “The Meadowlight Lamp is a standard desk lamp sold for offices. The catalog describes it as independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency and recommends it for sustainable office upgrades.”
- Evidence available: only that single catalog description in memory. I do not have the certificate, technical spec sheet, or provenance details in memory.

Claims that require verification (Meadowlight)
- “Independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency” — verify by requesting the certificate and identifying the certifier (ENERGY STAR, DesignLights Consortium (DLC), EU ecolabel, or another lab). Confirm test report and certification number.
- Power and efficacy claims — verify watts, lumens, and lumens per watt (LPW).
- Photometric performance — confirm delivered lux at desk height, beam distribution and any integrated shielding/glare control.
- Color and visual quality — verify color temperature(s) (K) and CRI (should be ≥80, ≥90 for color-critical tasks).
- Controls and features — confirm whether it is dimmable, has tunable white, occupancy sensor, and standby power.
- Warranty, expected lifetime (L70 hours), and replacement/repair policy.
- Price and availability for the required quantities.

Selection metrics I recommend (use these to compare Meadowlight vs others)
- Efficacy: ≥80–100 lumens per watt (LPW) for LED task lamps (higher is better).
- Delivered illuminance: ~300–500 lux at typical desktop working distance for general tasks.
- Color temperature: 3500–4000 K for most office tasks; consider tunable 2700–5000 K for flexible spaces.
- CRI: ≥80 (≥90 if color accuracy is important).
- Dimming: smooth dimming to low levels without flicker.
- Controls: desk-level controls + anti-glare design; occupancy or daylight sensors add savings.
- Standby power: as low as possible (<0.5 W) for networked/smart lamps.
- Lifetime/warranty: L70 ≥25,000–50,000 hours and a multi-year warranty (3–5 years preferred).
- Certifications: ENERGY STAR, DLC or equivalent lab test reports.

How to verify quickly
1. Ask procurement or the catalog owner for the Meadowlight spec sheet and the independent certification document(s). Look for certifier name and certificate number.
2. Confirm these specific data fields: nominal input watts, lumens, LPW, CCT, CRI, L70 hours, dimming type, warranty length.
3. If you want a second opinion, compare Meadowlight to ENERGY STAR or DLC-listed desk lamps (manufacturer + model) and compare LPW, lux at desk height, and warranty.

If you want next steps I can take
- Retrieve full Meadowlight specs and provenance from your catalog/procurement system (I tried memory and only found the brief catalog note).
- Search publicly for Meadowlight certification (ENERGY STAR/DLC listings) and datasheets.
- Pull 2–3 benchmark alternatives (ENERGY STAR/DLC certified desk/task lamps) and produce a short comparison (efficacy, lux, CCT, CRI, price, warranty, and which claims need verification).

Which of these would you like me to do next? Also tell me approximate budget per lamp and how many units you plan to buy — that helps narrow recommendations.
